items.review_rationale: Read accumulation point of a sequence using infinitely many visiting indices inside each neighborhood, counting repeated occurrences separately from distinct set values.

references.context: Mapping from natural-number index set to topological space X; repeated values allowed.
For any open U containing x, set of n satisfying x_n∈U is infinite.

references.disposition: Repeated sequence values count at distinct indices, unlike set accumulation definition.

items.review_rationale: Read accumulation of subset at a point via closure of A minus the point, requiring every neighborhood to meet A at another point.

references.context: Members of A other than x, whether or not x belongs to A.
For all neighborhoods U of x, U intersect (A\{x}) is nonempty.

references.phrase: set-accumulation distinct from sequence index accumulation
references.disposition: Requires distinct spatial points rather than infinitely many repeated visits.

items.review_rationale: Read Bell number B_n as count of partitions of any n-element set into disjoint nonempty blocks, including unique empty partition for n=0.

references.context: Set containing precisely n distinct elements.
Count of all equivalence classes of set partitions of n-element set.

references.disposition: Empty set has exactly one partition, the empty family of blocks.

items.review_rationale: Read convex hull as all finite convex combinations with strictly positive weights adding to 1, and explicit empty input convention.

references.phrase: finite convex combination with strictly positive coefficients
references.context: Sum of m≥1 terms λ_j u_j, each λ_j>0, total Σ λ_j=1.
Convention conv(∅)=∅ since no nonempty finite convex combination is available.

references.phrase: strict positivity not a restriction on convex hull
references.disposition: Zero-weight terms can be omitted from a finite convex combination.
